priorStories.headline: France says 410,000 joined nationwide protests
priorStories.body:
France’s Interior Ministry estimated that 410,000 people joined demonstrations across the country; organizers put the turnout at nearly 800,000.

Clashes broke out as protests ended in Paris, Marseille and several other cities. Police used tear gas and water cannons, and the interior minister said nearly 1,000 people were arrested. Two people were seriously injured, while some businesses were vandalized or looted.

priorStories.headline: New York archdiocese agrees to $800 million settlement
priorStories.body:
The Archdiocese of New York and lawyers for about 1,300 people who alleged sexual abuse by clergy or other church personnel reached an $800 million settlement agreement.

The agreement still requires signatures, which are scheduled for the week of November 6. Its terms also call for the release of documents concerning alleged offenders.

priorStories.headline: Houthis fire missiles toward Saudi Arabia and Aden
priorStories.body:
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed ballistic missiles heading toward Yanbu and Taif as Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed a wider attack on Saudi airports, oil facilities and other infrastructure. Saudi authorities had not confirmed that the claimed targets were hit.

Yemen’s internationally recognized government separately said three Houthi missiles struck coast guard sites in Aden. No casualties were immediately reported.

priorStories.headline: Typhoon Champi injures 527 people in Taiwan
priorStories.body:
Taiwan’s emergency operations center said Typhoon Champi left one person dead and 527 injured. Most injuries were linked to falling trees, power cables and billboards, as well as damaged water pipes.

The weather agency later downgraded Champi to a tropical storm and lifted its land warning.

candidates.summary: A bus collided with a truck on the Nairobi-Mombasa highway in Makueni County on Sunday morning, killing at least 22 people, police said. Several others were injured, and the county commissioner said the death toll could rise. Authorities had not determined the cause of the crash.
candidates.title: Kenya bus crash kills at least 22 people

candidates.summary: Saudi Arabia's military said air defenses intercepted Houthi missiles and drones directed toward Riyadh and southern parts of the country early Sunday. King Khalid International Airport also reopened terminals for domestic and international flights after earlier Houthi attacks had disrupted operations.
candidates.title: Saudi Arabia reports new Houthi attacks as Riyadh airport reopens

candidates.summary: The Israeli military announced restrictions barring Palestinian laborers from jobs in Israeli settlements and closed several West Bank crossings as it continued an operation launched after two Israeli soldiers were killed in Hebron on Friday.
candidates.title: Israel imposes new West Bank restrictions during military operation

candidates.summary: Voting began in Serbia's snap parliamentary election, with long lines reported outside polling stations. About 6.4 million voters were eligible to choose among 18 lists competing for the 250-seat National Assembly, in a close contest between Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party and the student-backed Students' List.
candidates.title: Serbia votes in closely contested parliamentary election

candidates.summary: Bulgarians began voting to elect a president from a record field of 27 candidates. Incumbent President Iliana Yotova and former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov were regarded as the leading contenders, with a runoff considered likely because the winner must secure a majority and turnout must exceed 50%.
candidates.title: Bulgaria holds presidential election

candidates.summary: Brazilians began voting in a presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro finished more than 2.2 million votes ahead of Lula in the first round, but neither secured a majority. Polls opened at 8 a.m. Brasília time and were scheduled to close at 5 p.m.
candidates.title: Brazil votes in presidential runoff

candidates.summary: Ukrainian officials disputed Elon Musk's assertion that Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms by using the civilian satellite service for offensive drone strikes. Presidential defense technology adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said longstanding restrictions made that use impossible. Musk acknowledged Saturday that SpaceX had throttled Starlink in Ukraine; Ukrainian officials said speed restrictions affecting Starlink and the military-focused Starshield service were lifted Saturday.
candidates.title: Ukraine disputes Musk's claim over military use of Starlink

candidates.summary: Brazil's presidential runoff encountered a late change after Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin ordered voting extended by up to two hours amid reported transportation and weather disruptions. The electoral court later clarified that voting would continue only at locations where polls had not already closed at 5 p.m.; stations that had closed were not reopened.
candidates.title: Brazil runoff receives partial two-hour voting extension

candidates.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election advanced to a November 1 runoff between incumbent Iliana Yotova and former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov. Exit polls placed Yotova narrowly ahead, with neither candidate securing the majority required for a first-round victory.
candidates.title: Bulgaria presidential election heads to runoff

candidates.summary: Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia's parliamentary election, saying preliminary sampling showed the student-led Students' List had won and was projected to receive 135 to 140 of parliament's 250 seats. Final official results remained pending.
candidates.title: Vucic concedes Serbia election to student-led movement

candidates.summary: Marine Le Pen formally launched her campaign for France's 2027 presidential election at a National Rally gathering in Orléans. She proposed tighter immigration controls, automatic expulsion of foreign criminals, lower business taxes and limits on European Union influence. Jordan Bardella was re-elected as the party's president and presented as her preferred prime minister.
candidates.title: Marine Le Pen formally launches French presidential campaign

candidates.summary: Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing for purchases of graphics processing units expected to arrive in the first and second quarters of 2027. Musk said revenue from Starlink and launch operations, along with the company's investment-grade status, helped maintain access to credit.
candidates.title: SpaceX closes $40 billion debt financing for GPUs

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile attacks had been fully restored after recent disruptions. He also said SpaceX's military-focused Starshield service had operated without the earlier speed restriction since Saturday morning, attributing both changes to discussions with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff.
candidates.title: Zelenskyy says U.S. ballistic-missile warnings fully restored

candidates.summary: Brazil's electoral court declared President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reelected to a fourth nonconsecutive term, with 51.79% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.21%. Bolsonaro refused to concede and said he would seek annulment over the late extension of voting at polling places that remained open. The electoral court's president said the extension did not affect the result.
candidates.title: Lula wins fourth term as Bolsonaro rejects Brazil result

candidates.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after nearly a year abroad. She appeared at a church in Lara state before traveling toward Caracas, where supporters gathered to greet her.
candidates.title: María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela

candidates.summary: Uganda's Health Ministry announced that citizens returning with a history of travel to the Democratic Republic of Congo must undergo 21 days of quarantine at their own expense. Authorities also intensified traveler screening at Entebbe International Airport and land crossings as precautions against Ebola, while saying Uganda remained free of confirmed cases.
candidates.title: Uganda tightens Ebola precautions for travelers from Congo

candidates.summary: A large fire at a Pacific Seafood processing plant in Newport, Oregon, prompted evacuation orders around the facility because it contained anhydrous ammonia. State officials said the ammonia tank did not appear punctured or leaking, and no injuries were reported. Firefighters and a hazardous-materials team remained at the scene.
candidates.title: Seafood plant fire prompts evacuations in Newport, Oregon

candidates.summary: Thousands of people rallied in central Prague against the Czech government's proposed overhaul of public television and radio funding. The demonstration followed lawmakers' initial approval of legislation that would replace license-fee financing with state-budget funding, which protesters and opposition parties said could expose the broadcasters to political pressure.
candidates.title: Thousands protest Czech public-media funding overhaul
